newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Concord Land seen weak on Thursday debut.
newsitem.headline: Concord Land seen weak on Thursday debut.

text.p: Concord Land Development Co Ltd shares are poised for a weak market debut on Thursday, with the poor response to the company's initial public offering (IPO) likely to prompt an early selloff, analysts said on Tuesday.

"It is possible that the shares will fall below their issue price as investors who subscribed to the shares are likely to liquidate their position on the debut," said Lennon Chan, executive director of Tai Fook Securities.
Concord Land is the Hong Kong and China property division of Pacific Concord Holdings Ltd.

The company offered 300 million shares at HK$3.48 per share, of which 85 percent was placed with institutional investors and 15 percent was offered in Hong Kong. The Hong Kong IPO was 1.53 times subscribed.
"We expect the share to come under selling pressure in view of the low subscription level," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.

Analysts said Concord Land also had to compete with three other upcoming new listings -- Arts Optical International Holdings Ltd, China Resources Beijing Land and Anhui Expressway Co Ltd -- which had taken some interest away from the issue.
However, some analysts said the downside would be limited.
"We don't expect the shares to fall very much because the shares are priced at a reasonable level of about a 30 percent discount to NAV (net asset value)," said one analyst at a local brokerage.
Concord Land is engaged in property development, mainly retail properties and shopping malls, in major cities in China.
